findings.highlight: My ignorance led me to the doorstep of this store once more.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はまた、馬鹿の一つ覚えみたいに、この店へと辿り着く。
findings.explanation: 馬鹿の一つ覚え means doing the same one thing like a fool who knows no other trick. Haruki has reflexively returned to the same gift shop; his ignorance does not lead him there. The English replaces self-mocking repetition with an invented causal character flaw.
findings.japanese:
俺はまた、馬鹿の一つ覚えみたいに、
この店へと辿り着く。
findings.todokanai: My ignorance led me to the doorstep of this store once more.

findings.highlight: Sorry for replying to you so late.
findings.evidenceJa: 『すいません、遅れます』
findings.explanation: Haruki's message says 'I'm sorry, I'll be late.' It does not apologize for a delayed reply. This is the notice that he will miss Mari's arrival and meet her only after seeing Setsuna, so the English changes the practical content of the message.
findings.japanese: 『すいません、遅れます』
findings.todokanai: "Sorry for replying to you so late."

findings.highlight: I can't repeat the mistake I made three years ago.
findings.evidenceJa: 三年前の非道を繰り返すわけにはいかないんです。
findings.explanation: Haruki calls his act three years ago 非道, inhuman cruelty; the English reduces it to a mistake.
findings.japanese: 三年前の非道を繰り返すわけにはいかないんです。
findings.todokanai: I can't repeat the mistake I made three years ago.

findings.highlight: If only I had rushed to give her my present immediately after buying it, just like what I've just done…
findings.evidenceJa: もしもあの日、プレゼントを買ったのが、今日みたいに時間ギリギリだったなら。
findings.explanation: Haruki wishes that three years earlier he had bought the present at the last possible moment, as he did today. The English instead says he wishes he had rushed to give it to Setsuna after buying it, altering the first condition in his chain of alternate-history causes.
findings.japanese:
もしもあの日、プレゼントを買ったのが、
今日みたいに時間ギリギリだったなら。
findings.todokanai: If only I had rushed to give her my present immediately after buying it, just like what I've just done…

findings.highlight: Regardless of my intention for seeking Kazusa out back then
findings.evidenceJa: 求める理由にどんな裏があろうとも、その想いだけは誰が何と言おうと本気だった。
findings.explanation: The omitted object is Setsuna from the preceding line: Haruki wanted Setsuna, and whatever ulterior motives lay behind wanting her, that feeling was real. The English substitutes Kazusa, reversing the woman whose sincerity this counterfactual is meant to establish.
findings.japanese:
求める理由にどんな裏があろうとも、
その想いだけは誰が何と言おうと本気だった。
findings.todokanai: Regardless of my intention for seeking Kazusa out back then, that feeling I had was real, no matter what anyone says.

findings.highlight: she'll continue telling me that she doesn't know anything until I spell it out to her
findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんとわかってるのに、俺がはっきり口に出すまでは、自分は何もわかってないって言ってもいい。
findings.explanation: Haruki says that under the social rule Setsuna clings to, she is entitled to say she does not know until he states the breakup explicitly. The English says she will actively keep telling him she knows nothing, turning a fragile procedural refuge into a planned lie.
findings.japanese:
ちゃんとわかってるのに、
俺がはっきり口に出すまでは、
自分は何もわかってないって言ってもいい。
findings.todokanai: Despite knowing full well about those facts, she'll continue telling me that she doesn't know anything until I spell it out to her.

findings.highlight: under the haze of alcohol
findings.evidenceJa: 酒が見せた哀しい幻影だって、そう、思い込むしかない。
findings.explanation: Haruki decides to treat the self-destructive Setsuna before him as a sad apparition produced by her drinking. The English locates the alcohol haze in Haruki's own act of seeing, even though he declined alcohol and Setsuna is the one who drank herself into this state.
findings.japanese:
酒が見せた哀しい幻影だって、
そう、思い込むしかない。
findings.todokanai: …And she's merely a sorrowful illusion I'm seeing under the haze of alcohol.

findings.highlight: It's snowing, just like it did back then three years ago.
findings.evidenceJa: 三年前のあの時は、雪だった。ぬかるんだ心に足をとられ、つまづいた。
findings.explanation: The present sky is cold and clear with stars. Haruki says that three years earlier it was snowing, then metaphorically says his feet were caught in his muddied heart and he stumbled. The English falsely makes it snow now and turns the inner mud into a current physical slip, breaking both chronology and image.
findings.japanese:
三年前のあの時は、雪だった。
ぬかるんだ心に足をとられ、つまづいた。
findings.todokanai: It's snowing, just like it did back then three years ago. My wavering heart causes my feet to slip and stumble forward.

findings.highlight: I've spent almost 100000 yen just for this
findings.evidenceJa: 会社の金じゃないんだぞ、自費で帰ってきたんだぞ…今度は１０万どころの騒ぎじゃなかったんだぞ…っ
findings.explanation: Mari says the self-funded emergency return was not remotely a mere 100,000-yen matter—it cost far more. The English says she spent almost 100,000 yen, inverting the stated scale of her sacrifice.
findings.japanese:
「会社の金じゃないんだぞ、
自費で帰ってきたんだぞ…
今度は１０万どころの騒ぎじゃなかったんだぞ…っ」
findings.todokanai: "I wasn't paid by the company for this, you know. I paid to come back here on my own… You know that I've spent almost 100000 yen just for this, right…?"

findings.highlight: almost as important as you are
findings.evidenceJa: 「俺にとって、麻理さんと同じくらい大切な人の」
findings.explanation: Haruki calls Setsuna someone as important to him as Mari, 同じくらい. 'Almost as important' creates a hierarchy absent from the confession and softens precisely the equality that makes the disclosure devastating.
findings.japanese: 「俺にとって、麻理さんと同じくらい大切な人の」
findings.todokanai: "She's someone important to me, almost as important as you are, Mari-san…"

findings.highlight: forced myself to look their way
findings.evidenceJa: 心の行き場をなくし、近くの優しさにすがりつき、無理やり俺に向けさせようとした。
findings.explanation: Haruki says his stranded heart clung to nearby kindness and tried to force that kindness—Mari's feelings—to turn toward him. The English instead says he forced himself to look toward her, reversing the coercive direction in his self-indictment.
findings.japanese:
心の行き場をなくし、近くの優しさにすがりつき、
無理やり俺に向けさせようとした。
findings.todokanai: There was no place for my heart to go, so I chose to tightly cling onto the closest act of kindness and forced myself to look their way.

findings.highlight: as if to blow a gust of fresh air to bequeath my flustered self
findings.evidenceJa: そんな、俺の焦燥なんか何処吹く風みたいに、麻理さんがゆっくり立ち上がる。
findings.explanation: 何処吹く風 means acting as though another person's agitation is no concern of yours. Mari slowly stands as if Haruki's panic means nothing to her. The English decomposes the idiom into an incoherent literal gust of air that she somehow 'bequeaths' him.
findings.japanese:
そんな、俺の焦燥なんか何処吹く風みたいに、
麻理さんがゆっくり立ち上がる。
findings.todokanai: Mari-san slowly stood up, as if to blow a gust of fresh air to bequeath my flustered self.

findings.highlight: you weren't serious, now, were you?
findings.evidenceJa: 「メールの件、正気じゃないよな？」
findings.explanation: The editor asks whether Mari is sane—正気. She replies that she had hoped he would ask whether she was serious—本気. Rendering both words as 'serious' erases the one-character contrast and the joke that he treats her decision as insanity rather than mere bluffing.
findings.japanese: 「メールの件、正気じゃないよな？」
findings.todokanai: "About the email you sent me, you weren't serious, now, were you?"

findings.highlight: "Thank you very much. Just as you said, please allow me to do it."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ありがとうございます。
おっしゃる通り、のびのびやらせてもらってます」
findings.explanation: Mari says she has indeed been allowed to work freely; the English turns this into a request, 'please allow me to do it.'
findings.japanese:
「ありがとうございます。
おっしゃる通り、のびのびやらせてもらってます」
findings.todokanai: "Thank you very much. Just as you said, please allow me to do it."

findings.highlight: "In any case, I can't really refuse this arrangement given it's something that's decided by the company, and I have no reason to decline it at all since it's what I wished for in the first place. …And the truth is, it's something that I've decided on quite a while ago."
findings.evidenceJa:
「何しろ会社の人事だから断れるはずもないし、
そもそも希望通りだから断る理由もないし、
…実は結構前から決まってたし、な」
findings.explanation: The transfer had been decided quite some time ago, impersonal/company-side; the English says it is something Mari herself decided on.
findings.japanese:
「何しろ会社の人事だから断れるはずもないし、
そもそも希望通りだから断る理由もないし、
…実は結構前から決まってたし、な」
findings.todokanai: "In any case, I can't really refuse this arrangement given it's something that's decided by the company, and I have no reason to decline it at all since it's what I wished for in the first place. …And the truth is, it's something that I've decided on quite a while ago."

findings.highlight: it actually feels quite refreshing
findings.evidenceJa: あ～あ…何もかもぶちまけたら、正直、どうでも良くなってきたよ…
findings.explanation: After everything has been spilled, Mari says she is honestly starting not to care about any of it. The English calls the disclosure refreshing, replacing bitter emotional disengagement with positive catharsis.
findings.japanese:
「あ～あ…何もかもぶちまけたら、
正直、どうでも良くなってきたよ…」
findings.todokanai: "Aa-ah… to be honest, now that we've finally told each other everything, it actually feels quite refreshing…"

findings.highlight: She willingly embraced me
findings.evidenceJa: 異動のことをずっと黙ったまま、俺に抱かれた…？
findings.explanation: Haruki realizes that Mari let him take her or make love to her while concealing the transfer. The English makes Mari the one who embraced him, reversing the grammatical and sexual agency in the thought that triggers his sense of betrayal.
findings.japanese:
異動のことをずっと黙ったまま、
俺に抱かれた…？
findings.todokanai: She willingly embraced me while being silent about her impending transfer all the while…?

findings.highlight: told me she would sleep with me
findings.evidenceJa: 俺と、寝たって言うのか？
findings.explanation: Haruki asks in disbelief whether she slept with him while knowing she would leave him. The English invents a statement that she would sleep with him, changing a completed sexual relationship into a verbal future promise.
findings.japanese: 俺と、寝たって言うのか？
findings.todokanai: And told me she would sleep with me despite that?

findings.highlight: Before I knew it, I'd gotten so close to Mari-san that my hand could reach her.
findings.evidenceJa:
いつの間にか、麻理さんの手の届く範囲にまで
近づいていた。
findings.explanation: Haruki has moved within Mari's reach; the English says his hand can reach her, reversing the possessor and duplicating the next line.
findings.japanese:
いつの間にか、麻理さんの手の届く範囲にまで
近づいていた。
findings.todokanai: Before I knew it, I'd gotten so close to Mari-san that my hand could reach her.

findings.highlight: She stopped before she could slap me for the fourth time.
findings.evidenceJa: 四発目は、直前で止まった。俺が、止めた。
findings.explanation: The fourth blow stops just before landing because Haruki stops it. The English first says Mari stopped herself, then immediately says Haruki stopped her, producing an internally contradictory action and briefly assigning the decisive resistance to the wrong person.
findings.japanese:
四発目は、直前で止まった。
俺が、止めた。
findings.todokanai: She stopped before she could slap me for the fourth time. And I was the one who stopped her.

findings.highlight: Mari-san easily slaps me out of my attempt to run away from reality.
findings.evidenceJa:
そんな俺の現実逃避を、
麻理さんはしっかり見破っていた。
findings.explanation: Mari sees through Haruki's flight into cleaning; the English says she 'slaps' him out of it despite no physical action here.
findings.japanese:
そんな俺の現実逃避を、
麻理さんはしっかり見破っていた。
findings.todokanai: Mari-san easily slaps me out of my attempt to run away from reality.

findings.highlight: You… were my…
findings.evidenceJa: 「じゃあな、北原。私はお前が…お前のこと…」
findings.explanation: Mari begins 'I, you… about you…' and cannot complete what is plainly tending toward a confession before retreating in line 698. The English supplies past tense and a possessive construction ('You were my…'), making Haruki answer 'I was your?' and forcing a specific utterance that the Japanese deliberately leaves broken.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあな、北原。
私はお前が…お前のこと…」
findings.todokanai: "Goodbye, Kitahara. You… were my…"

findings.highlight: "I was… your?"
findings.evidenceJa: 「俺の…こと？」
findings.explanation: Haruki repeats only 'Me…?' after Mari's broken start; the English has him ask 'I was… your?' to match its invented possessive construction.
findings.japanese: 「俺の…こと？」
findings.todokanai: "I was… your?"
